name: Abiathar
bio:
Abiathar was the son of the priest Ahimelech. When Saul, acting on Doeg's report, ordered the massacre of the priests of Nob, Abiathar alone escaped, fleeing to David with an ephod in hand (1 Samuel 22:20; 23:6). He told David that Saul had slaughtered his father's household; David, grief-stricken, said, "That day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, I knew he would be sure to tell Saul... I am responsible for the death of your whole family," and promised him protection: "Stay with me; don't be afraid. The man who wants to kill you is trying to kill me too. You will be safe with me" (1 Samuel 22:21-23).

From then on, Abiathar stayed close to David, carrying the ephod as the priest through whom David inquired of the LORD during his years as a fugitive — as at Keilah, where David used the ephod Abiathar brought to learn of Saul's plan to besiege the city (1 Samuel 23:6-12). Once David's kingdom was secure, Abiathar served alongside Zadok as priest in David's royal administration (2 Samuel 8:17).

When Absalom's rebellion forced David to flee Jerusalem, Abiathar went out with Zadok and the ark, but David sent the priests back into the city, choosing to trust the LORD's will rather than treat the ark as a talisman for his own safety. David asked Abiathar, along with his son Jonathan, to stay behind and relay to him anything they could learn of Absalom's plans (2 Samuel 15:24-29, 35-36). After Hushai's counsel defeated Ahithophel's advice to pursue David at once, Hushai brought word to Zadok and Abiathar, who sent their sons to warn David to cross the Jordan immediately (2 Samuel 17:15-22). After Absalom's death, David sent word through Abiathar and Zadok urging the elders of Judah not to be the last to bring the king back, helping to tip Judah's loyalty back to David (2 Samuel 19:11-14). Abiathar remained one of David's priests through Sheba's revolt (2 Samuel 20:25). As David grew old, Abiathar backed Adonijah's bid for the throne alongside Joab, while Zadok remained loyal to David — but Solomon was crowned instead, ending the attempt (1 Kings 1:7, 19, 25). After David's death, when Adonijah's request to marry Abishag revealed a renewed claim to the throne, Solomon removed Abiathar from the priesthood for good, sparing his life only because he had carried the ark before David and shared in all his father's hardships, and banished him to his hometown of Anathoth. Scripture notes this fulfilled the LORD's long-standing word against the house of Eli spoken at Shiloh — Abiathar being the last priest descended from Eli's line (1 Kings 2:26-27), bringing to an end the family Abiathar had represented ever since fleeing Saul's massacre at Nob as a young man.
